headline: Good morning — Wall Street steadied after a sharp tech sell-off, while Australia's government faces pressure over another RBA rate rise and Victoria's Big Build royal commission opens.

highlights.label: Wall Street
highlights.text: US shares ended mixed on Friday after Thursday's steep AI-led sell-off; the S&P 500 still lost about 2.7% for the week.

highlights.label: Rates pressure
highlights.text: Another RBA rate rise has put the Albanese government under pressure, with the budget and cost of living in focus.

highlights.label: Big Build inquiry
highlights.text: A royal commission into Victoria's $100 billion Big Build holds its first public hearing today.

tip.title: Keep a steady wake-up time
tip.body: Getting up at about the same time each day, including weekends, helps anchor the body clock and makes sleep more regular. Pair it with a dimmer, screen-free half hour before bed tonight.

quote.text: Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
quote.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

items.title: What Salesforce's Braze deal means for Marketing Cloud users
items.summary: Salesforce announced on 20 October a deal to buy customer engagement platform Braze for about US$5.66 billion. Closing is not expected before February 2027, so Marketing Cloud customers face a long period of roadmap uncertainty.

items.title: Gmail's AI inbox may change how deliverability works
items.summary: The piece argues that Gemini-powered inbox summaries mean email must persuade the AI to surface it, not only the reader. Older than 48 hours, but still relevant to email teams.

items.title: Email deliverability changes to watch in 2026
items.summary: A roundup reports Spamhaus is phasing in HELO and reverse DNS checks on sending IPs from November 2026, alongside stricter Gmail rejection behaviour. Vendor-published and not independently confirmed; senders should check their DNS setup.

items.title: Salesforce to buy Braze for about US$5.66 billion
items.summary: Salesforce agreed to acquire Braze for US$47.50 per share in cash, aiming to strengthen Marketing Cloud's cross-channel personalisation. The deal is the largest recent signal of Salesforce's marketing strategy.

items.title: Salesforce signs deal to acquire Loops
items.summary: Salesforce's newsroom lists the Loops AI analytics acquisition, which is intended to be folded into Tableau. Details beyond the newsroom listing were not independently checked.

items.title: Dreamforce 2026: the top 10 announcements
items.summary: A recap of Dreamforce announcements, including Hyperforce running natively on Google Cloud, with general availability slated for November 2026 in North America. Published earlier than the last 48 hours.

items.title: Salesforce reports 29,000 Agentforce deals
items.summary: Salesforce said in February 2026 it had reached 29,000 Agentforce deals. Older story included because nothing newer with a verified link was found.

sfstatus.statusNote: No active Salesforce incidents were found in a third-party tracker; status.salesforce.com was not checked directly, so confirm there for APAC instances.

items.title: Albanese under pressure at home as he attends CHOGM
items.summary: The Prime Minister is representing Australia at the Commonwealth summit while domestic issues mount, including another interest rate rise. The trip is being questioned as households feel the squeeze.

items.title: Bleak RBA outlook complicates budget tightening
items.summary: Analysis argues the RBA's gloomy outlook means this may not be the time for sharp budget cuts. The debate is shaping the government's pitch for savings measures.

items.title: Albanese links Iran war to US midterm result
items.summary: The Prime Minister said economic pain and the Middle East conflict contributed to the US midterm outcome and called for de-escalation. He later said he would deal with President Trump respectfully on Iran.

items.title: Federal politics live: digital duty of care and savings measures
items.summary: Parliament returns with the government urging the opposition to back savings measures. The live blog also covers a bushfire risk package.

items.title: Victoria's Big Build royal commission begins hearings
items.summary: A royal commission into integrity in major public construction projects holds its first public hearing, centred on allegations around the $100 billion Big Build. It could shape how Victoria delivers infrastructure.

items.title: Modi spends Diwali with security forces in Bastar
items.summary: The Prime Minister marked Diwali with security personnel and said the end of Maoist violence reflected sound policy and strong political will. The government announced on 31 March that the country was free of Naxalism.

items.title: Indian shares reported to surge as oil prices fall
items.summary: A newsletter reports the Sensex jumped more than 2,000 points on 6 November as oil eased. Index levels differ between sources and are not independently confirmed.

items.title: MPTC and ZPTC counting favours TDP
items.summary: Counting for local body polls on 7 November showed the TDP leading in many seats, with unanimous wins in 77 ZPTCs and 2,051 MPTCs. The results indicate the ruling alliance's grassroots strength.

items.title: Lokesh accuses Jagan of stirring trouble in Pulivendula
items.summary: Minister Nara Lokesh said the YSRCP leader created a law-and-order issue during local polls and then cast himself as a victim. He said polls were otherwise peaceful across the state.

items.title: Wall Street ends mixed after strong jobs data
items.summary: Chip and AI shares rebounded, with Nvidia up 3.9% and AMD up 10.8%, while a hot jobs report lifted rate-hike bets. Figures come from secondary recaps and may be revised.

items.title: Weekly summary: S&P 500 down about 2.7%
items.summary: The index trimmed but did not erase weekly losses after Thursday's sell-off of about 4.4%, linked to worries about tighter AI regulation. Breadth was weak, with decliners outnumbering advancers.

items.title: Stock market news for 6 November
items.summary: Yahoo's daily wrap covers the jobs data and tech swings. Traders now look to the next inflation (CPI) release.

items.title: ANZ posts $7.3 billion profit as Wall Street rebounds
items.summary: ANZ reported a full-year profit of $7.3 billion before the open. The ABC markets blog tracks the session.

items.title: ASX set to rise 0.2% after US rebound
items.summary: Futures point to a modest gain after a weak Friday. Gold miners may start quietly after gold fell overnight.

items.title: Five things to watch on the ASX 200 today
items.summary: A preview covering the ANZ result, oil near US$98 a barrel and US-Iran talks. Early-morning readings may have moved by the open.

items.title: Home values fall for a seventh month in October
items.summary: Cotality's national index reportedly fell 1.2% in October, with Brisbane down 2% and Sydney down 1.6%. Buyers remain largely absent.

items.title: Rate hike shrinks borrowing power
items.summary: Cotality estimates 2026's rate rises have cut a median-income household's borrowing capacity by roughly $90,000. The RBA's next decision is due 8 December, per one source; unconfirmed.

items.title: Auction clearance rates sit below 50%
items.summary: Cotality's preliminary national clearance rate fell to 50.3% in September, with final figures revised to 49.1%. Older than 48 hours, but shows weak auction demand.

items.title: Cotality September index: sixth monthly fall
items.summary: Home values fell 1.1% in September, with the downturn broadening across suburbs. Older report, useful context for the October decline.
